body:
Follow-up to #355. User approved full snekql transactions and SQLAlchemy ORM sessions.

Compare equivalent bounded integer-cent/positive-quantity validation, millisecond UTC timestamps, literal status defaults, and database CHECK constraints on SQLite and MariaDB. SQLAlchemy gets explicit validation/types; snekql gets hand-authored migrations. Record actual round trips, rejection stages, defaults, raw SQL behavior, and schema verification limits.

Deliver an independent research report, runnable examples, evidence, and focused test-first checks. No package fixes or merging previous research PRs. Qualitative conclusions must describe actual code and observed behavior, not usability scores.
title: Research equivalent runtime contracts and schema-rule maintenance versus SQLAlchemy
